target_customer: Businesses and brands such as restaurants, wineries, House of Blues and Joe's Jeans that wanted designed QR code campaigns
problem: Plain QR codes were ugly and went to ordinary web pages, so businesses lacked branded codes, landing pages and scan analytics.
business_model: freemium SaaS, paid plans from $25 per month, plus print services

founders.name: Hamilton Chan
previous_startups: Turned around his family's printing business
founders.background_notes: From the June 2011 TechCrunch article; YC page confirms Harvard and Harvard Law and adds corporate attorney.

competitors.name: Scan
competitors.what: Free QR and barcode scanning app and code generator
competitors.traction_then: app launched early 2011, 1 million downloads in three months per a later article

technical_complexity.rationale: Code generation, a CMS for landing pages, scan analytics and a free reader app are ordinary web and mobile work.

defensibility.rationale: Printed codes pointing at Paperlinks pages created some lock-in, but generators were plentiful.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Scan raised money in 2012 and named Paperlinks its closest competitor; no source says what happened to Paperlinks.

market_need_then: TechCrunch (June 2011) reported sales doubling every month, about 2,000 QR campaigns in three months, and customers including House of Blues and Joe's Jeans.

branding.domain_note: Company site paperlinks.com per the YC page; the YC directory slug and name is PayDragon, which no source explains.

identity.logo: not described in any source found
identity.visual_style: Designer QR codes that can embed a logo

brand_strength.rationale: Descriptive name fit the product and appeared in several launch articles, but no brand community or lasting recognition shows up.

outcome_analysis: Paperlinks sold designed QR codes and landing pages and showed fast early growth in 2011 with named brand customers, but no later funding, exit or shutdown account was found, so the reason it became inactive is not public. QR codes also faced a weak consumer habit in the US, but no source states that as the cause.
notes: paperlinks.com returned HTTP 503 so the site is treated as unavailable. TechCrunch (June 2011) says Y Combinator was the only money raised so far and the company planned to accept Start Fund money; no amount or later round found, so funding is none_found rather than zero. The Scan source is dated February 2012, about six months after the batch, and is the only dated rival found; Delivr appeared undated and is not listed. A SoCal Tech interview dated February 2011 shows the company existed before the batch.
